messages:
sarah-cs: Scheduling a dedicated-capacity priming rehearsal for Meridian (customer) next Tue 14:00 PDT / 21:00 UTC. Objective: validate committed quota, exercise autoscale, and run short failure scenarios. Need owners and a short playbook for the customer enablement call.
diego-ops: I can own reservations + infra changes. Proposed reserved GPUs = 8 for the window (pad +2 for safety). Will tag everything with `meridian-jan-reserve`.
anya-ml: We should test two model profiles: Meridian-H-3b (default) and Meridian-H-3b-quant (fallback). For the main run, we'll simulate mixed route traffic: 70% realtime chat small payloads, 20% long completion, 10% embeddings.
kevin-sre: Plan to run a staggered ramp: 10m smoke, 20m 50% load, 20m 100% load, 10m soak. We'll also run a short packet-loss fault injection (1% loss) for 5 minutes during the soak to validate graceful degradation.
sarah-cs: Customer-facing enablement: quick 10-min walkthrough at 13:30 PDT with their infra lead + app owner. Checklist items: how to read per-route latency, how to ask for exclusions, who to ping for immediate failover.
talia-eng: I'll add a mini-runbook to the repo and include commands to change routing and to enable the quant fallback. Snippet: ```bash
# switch route to fallback pool
redwood route update --route app/meridian/realtime --pool horizon-quant --rate-limit 0.8
```
Also include rollback: `redwood route update --route app/meridian/realtime --pool horizon-default`
deploy-bot: deploy:infra changes merged to branch meridian/reserve (CI: passed). https://ci.redwood/internal/meridian/1234
diego-ops: Quick quota question: finance gave committed_units in GPU-hours. I propose we publish an expected QPS per GPU metric in the customer summary (e.g., ~30 QPS per GPU @ 512-token median). That will help correlate their expected peak to reserved hours.
anya-ml: Add KV prefix warmup for top 5k prefixes and an initial batch warmup so we don't hit cold-KV tails. I'll provide the warm script. Also will capture batch-size histogram for the run.
kevin-sre: Monitoring checklist: p50/p95/p99, 5xx rate, GPU mem/SM utilization, batching distribution, KV hit ratio, and request retry count. Alert thresholds: p95 > 350ms for >3m or 5xx > 0.5% for >2m triggers pager.
sarah-cs: Renewal risk framing: post-test we'll produce a one-line status (green/amber/red) + short rationale for the AM that owns renewal. Include cost implications and any perf delta compared to SLO.
diego-ops: I'll create the terraform diff and reserve the GPUs. ETA for diffs: EOD today. Will also provide a cost delta estimate: expected additional $Xk for the reserved window (will compute).
talia-eng: For the load generator, use this command: ```bash
python -m rl_load --routes-file meridian-mix.json --duration 60 --target-qps 320 --warm-prefix 5000
```
We have a route mix file that mirrors production route proportions.
anya-ml: Post-run ML checks: run two evaluation prompt suites (safety & quality) against both default and quant models. If any regression > 2% on safety/intent, flag for product.
kevin-sre: Ownership recap: Diego = reserve + infra, Talia = runbook & load scripts, Anya = perf & evals, Sarah = customer enablement + renewal note, Kevin = oncall & fallback runbook.
sarah-cs: Customer note for invite: "We will rehearse capacity priming with minimal impact; please share any routes to exempt by Mon 17:00 PDT." Add contact list and debrief at +30m after test.
diego-ops: One more ask: can we include per-1M-token cost estimate in the postmortem? Finance finds that helps with renewal conversations.
sarah-cs: Yes — include both GPU-hours and per-1M-token cost. Post-test deliverable: short deck slide + renewal risk line.
talia-eng: I'll add a Graf dashboard that shows cost, latency, and fallback switch timeline.
sarah-cs: Great, thanks team. I'll send the calendar invite and draft enablement note in #customer-comms. Ping here if anything changes. :raised_hands:
